canonical_statement: Let U be an open subset of the upper half-plane whose union with its reflection and its relative boundary interval on the real axis forms an open reflection-symmetric domain V. If u : U -> R is harmonic, continuous up to that interval, and is zero there, then the odd reflection u(z) for Im z >= 0 and -u(conj z) for Im z < 0 is harmonic on V and extends u.
domain_and_universes: Planar domains represented in Complex (equivalently Real x Real); real-valued functions; Prop in Lean universe 0
quantifiers: V : Set Complex, open and invariant under complex conjugation
u : Complex -> Real (used on U and its real-axis boundary)
hypotheses: conj-invariance: z in V iff conj z in V
u is continuous on U union {z in V | z.im = 0}
u z = 0 on {z in V | z.im = 0}
conclusion: The odd reflection is harmonic on V, agrees with u on U, and hence is a harmonic continuation across the real-axis portion of V.

alternate_encodings.target: holomorphic Schwarz reflection for a function real-valued on the boundary

excluded_degenerate_cases: No claim is made without an open two-sided reflected domain, continuity to the reflecting interval, or zero boundary values. Endpoints of an isolated boundary segment are not asserted to be interior continuation points.
